user_agreements.content:
# AI Factory Terms of Service

## 1. Acceptable Use

AI Factory resources are provided for legitimate AI/ML research, development, and production workloads.

## 2. GPU Resource Allocation

- Fair-share scheduling for shared GPU pools
- Dedicated GPU passthrough for intensive workloads
- vGPU/MIG partitioning for cost-effective inference

## 3. LLM Services

- Model inference endpoints are provided as-is
- Users must comply with model licensing terms (Llama, Mistral, etc.)
- Rate limits apply based on subscription tier

## 4. Prohibited Activities

- Cryptocurrency mining on GPU resources
- Training models for malicious purposes
- Unauthorized access to other tenants' resources
- Bypassing resource quotas or isolation

## 5. Data Responsibility

- Users are responsible for data privacy compliance
- Platform does not inspect or retain inference data
- Model outputs are not logged by default

# AI Factory Privacy Policy

## 1. Data Collection

We collect:
- Account and organization information
- Resource usage metrics (GPU hours, inference requests)
- System logs for troubleshooting

## 2. Inference Data

- API requests and responses are not logged
- Users retain full ownership of prompts and outputs
- Optional audit logging available upon request

## 3. Model Artifacts

- Custom fine-tuned models remain user property
- Secure deletion upon project termination
- Export functionality available

## 4. Usage Analytics

- Aggregated usage statistics for capacity planning
- No individual user profiling
- Opt-out available for non-essential metrics

offerings.getting_started:
## Getting Started with NVIDIA H100 GPU VM

### SSH Access
```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/your_key user@<vm-ip-address>
```

### Verify GPU
```bash
nvidia-smi
# Should show H100 with 80GB memory
```

### CUDA Environment
```bash
nvcc --version
# CUDA 12.4 pre-installed
```

### PyTorch Quick Start
```bash
conda activate pytorch
python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"
```

### Performance Tips
- Use BF16 for transformer training
- Enable Flash Attention 2 for memory efficiency
- Use NCCL for multi-GPU communication

### Support
GPU Support: gpu-support@ai-factory.example.com

offerings.getting_started:
## Getting Started with Llama 3.1 Inference

### API Endpoint
Your endpoint: `https://<resource-id>.llm.ai-factory.example.com/v1/`

### OpenAI-Compatible API
```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://<resource-id>.llm.ai-factory.example.com/v1/",
    api_key="your-api-key"
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

### cURL Example
```bash
curl -X POST "https://<endpoint>/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct", 
       "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

### Rate Limits
- Requests per minute: Based on plan
- Tokens per minute: Based on plan

### Support
LLM Support: llm-support@ai-factory.example.com

offerings.getting_started:
## Getting Started with AI-Ready Kubernetes

### Download Kubeconfig
1. Go to Resource Details
2. Download kubeconfig.yaml
3. Configure kubectl:
```bash
export KUBECONFIG=~/Downloads/kubeconfig.yaml
kubectl get nodes
```

### Verify GPU Nodes
```bash
kubectl get nodes -l nvidia.com/gpu.present=true
kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | grep nvidia.com/gpu
```

### Deploy GPU Workload
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: cuda
    image: nvidia/cuda:12.4-base
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    command: ["nvidia-smi"]
  restartPolicy: Never
```

### Kubeflow Access
If enabled, access at: `https://<cluster>.k8s.ai-factory.example.com/`

### Support
K8s Support: k8s-support@ai-factory.example.com

offerings.name: AI Model Storage
offerings.description: High-performance NVMe-backed storage optimized for AI workloads. Designed for model checkpoints, training datasets, and inference caches. Supports both POSIX filesystem access and S3-compatible object storage. Integrated with OpenNebula datastores for automatic provisioning. Managed by waldur-site-agent with OpenNebula backend.
offerings.getting_started:
## Getting Started with AI Model Storage

### POSIX Access
```bash
# Mount point (auto-mounted on GPU VMs)
/ai-storage/<project-name>/

# Subdirectories
/ai-storage/<project>/datasets/
/ai-storage/<project>/checkpoints/
/ai-storage/<project>/models/
```

### S3 Access
```bash
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<provided-key>
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<provided-secret>
export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=https://s3.ai-factory.example.com

aws s3 ls s3://<project-bucket>/
aws s3 cp model.safetensors s3://<project-bucket>/models/
```

### PyTorch Integration
```python
import torch

# Save checkpoint
torch.save(model.state_dict(), '/ai-storage/project/checkpoints/model_v1.pt')

# Load checkpoint
model.load_state_dict(torch.load('/ai-storage/project/checkpoints/model_v1.pt'))
```

### Performance Tips
- Use parallel data loading for large datasets
- Store checkpoints on High-Performance tier
- Archive completed experiments to Archive tier

### Support
Storage Support: storage-support@ai-factory.example.com

offerings.getting_started:
## Getting Started with OpenNebula VDC

### Access Sunstone
Login via SSO at your organization's Sunstone URL.
Your Keycloak account is automatically mapped to the correct VDC and role.

### Roles
- **Admin**: Full VDC management (groupadmin view)
- **User**: Standard VM operations (user view)
- **Cloud**: Simplified cloud interface (cloud view)

### Create a VM
1. Login to Sunstone via SAML/SSO
2. Navigate to VMs > Create
3. Select a template from your VDC
4. Configure resources within your quota
5. Deploy

### Quota Management
Resource quotas (CPU, RAM, storage) are managed through Waldur.
Contact your project manager to request quota changes.

### Support
VDC Support: vdc-support@ai-factory.example.com
